sections.content: The pronoun *se* lets you leave out who does the action, which is useful for rules, services and general workplace processes. With a noun, the verb agrees with it (passive *se*): *se busca una persona*, *se buscan personas*. With no noun, the verb stays singular (impersonal *se*): *se trabaja mucho aquí*.

items.spanish: Se busca una persona con experiencia en gestión de proyectos.
items.english: A person with project-management experience is wanted.

items.spanish: Se requiere experiencia profesional y buen nivel de inglés.
items.english: Professional experience and a good level of English are required.

items.spanish: Se permite trabajar desde casa dos días a la semana.
items.english: Working from home two days a week is permitted.

items.spanish: En esta oficina se organizan reuniones todos los lunes.
items.english: Meetings are organised in this office every Monday.

items.spanish: En esta oficina se trabaja mucho por la mañana.
items.english: In this office people work a lot in the morning.

sections.content: Use *se* when the agent is general or unknown. Singular noun, singular verb (*se organiza una reunión*); plural noun, plural verb (*se organizan reuniones*); no noun, singular verb (*se trabaja*).
